title: Bounded-error space-bounded acceptance
statement: A finite nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ decides a Boolean language $L$ in space bounded by $s$ with bounded error if $N$ uses space at most $s$ and, for every Boolean input $x$, there is a natural number $T$ such that $N$ halts on $x$ within $T$ steps and its probability of outputting the indicator of membership in $L$ is at least $2/3$.
hypotheses_covered: N uses space bounded by s
For every Boolean input x, there exists a natural number T
N halts on x within T steps
The probability that N outputs the membership indicator for L on x within T steps is at least 2/3
